Disclaimer Oru 5 pages-ku lengthy content irukkum. Please don't skip, as it has important insights about Tamizh. Just don't skip. Enakku theriyum evlo perusa potta yaarum padikka maatanga-nu, but irunthaalum please padikka.

Munadi sonna story ku ethachum vazhi iruka nu yosicha, naama yaarum tamizha digital purpose ku use panrathu illa, we all use English instead. First, ennake tamizh pidikathu sariyavum varathu. Watching anime and other language series/movies (except English movies) made me appreciate how they cherish and preserve their languages. They inspired me to start loving my mother tongue, Tamil. I even learned to write in Hangul (Korean), but as I didn't learn the language, just the script, I only know the characters. I also learned Hiragana and Katakana (Japanese) very well, but they are forgotten due to lack of usage. I learned them 2 years back.

Yes, we need English, but we shouldn't downgrade Tamil over English. Ithula ethana per mobile la Tamil default system language ah use panreenga? Only old people? Nope, everyone uses English. Tamizh la use pannalaamnu, first, Tamizh la switch panna, neenga tamizha irunthalum ungalukku puriyaathu, but puriyum use panna. It is good to use, but since no one uses it, oru sila idathula mattum it was not well optimized for it. The text and font are often too big, some parts are not translated, and there are other issues. These should be solved if the companies know people use it. But in other languages, for example, Korean and Chinese, they are well optimized because they use them everywhere

And how many of them store contacts in Tamizh? No one. All save like "amma" in Tamizh only, but in romanized Latin script. I noted another thing—eththana per thannoda signature ah English la podureengalo? There are two types: one is they are Tamizhs, and they know English very well, so they sign in English. Another, they don’t even know English; they know a little but still sign in English.  Everywhere in every place, except India (India-layum sila irukaanga), other countries, everyone signs in their own language. Our language is our identity, so why do we sign in English?

I noted another thing: there is no perfect Tamil font like in English. Every Tamil font has defects, but we write it symmetrically and it looks good. On screens, however, it doesn't look good. I've seen on the internet that Tamil font doesn't even look good everywhere. They are not symmetrical and pleasing to see. In some places, they are very big or too bold. But in Hindi, which uses the Devanagari script, it is very well optimized everywhere in digital areas. Korean and Japanese too are well optimized in digital devices.

We need to develop a new Tamil standard  font with some modifications. The Tamil font needs to be updated to look great on all devices, be easy to write, and more. I personally like the Hangeul script; it looks great but requires taking hands and placing without connectivity. It is a good script and simple. Tamil has a special property—all the letters are written with a single attempt. Our computer prodigy people should take efforts to make Tamil very easy, fast to type, and with features like autocorrect, all through an app to reach people. Our government should also take steps to introduce this to youngsters. The situation where people say, "Tamizh la type panna theriyathu. Thappa varum," should be eradicated.

Tamizh has 247 letters, while English has only 26 letters, making it easier. But Japanese has Hiragana, Katakana, and Kanji, three different scripts, and Chinese has around 3000 characters. If they can type easily, we should also find it easy. Likewise, the goods we export, the machines we manufacture, should have our language included. It shouldn't just be in English.

And lastly, piramozhigal thinikuranga solrom English Hindi la but athukaaga atha namma kathukama vitutona namaku than loss. Athulan adopt panikita namma career ku nallathu. Ippa English nalla pesuna, that's what is needed for survival. Treat English as a language, not as status and prestige.  Oru silar irukkanga, Tamizh's avanga tamizh kaatti padikka sonna theriyathu nu solluvaanga aana mother tongue tamilzhaam. But athukaaga thaaimozhi ya maranthura kudaathu. Athu namma pesura mozhi la illa tamizhargal na it can be defined in terms of there panbaadu kalachaaram avanga attire discipline. So, learning many languages is good. Not knowing mother tongue is not good.
